transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM); Raj Patel (Acme Platform), Lena Morales (Acme Cloud Architect), Tom Wu (SRE), Amira Lopez (Security)

Summary (auto): quick notes: deep dive on Private VPC networking and runtime perf; mix of networking and inference tradeoffs; customer needs to validate VPC layout and SSO/KMS notes.

[00:00:00] Jordan Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll jump in, Samira will walk through the runtime perf bits and I'll cover the PrivateLink/networking part.
[00:00:34] Raj Patel: thanks Jordan, yeah um quick context, we're evaluating Redwood Private for running inference in our AWS VPC, requirements are no public internet egress from the inference subnets, SOC2, and low 95th p99 latency for chat. We also have existing transit setup and peering to partner accounts.
[00:01:02] Samira Khan: great, yeah and we'll try to map those to config options. quick question, do you plan on using our managed control plane over PrivateLink or the fully air-gapped on-prem package?
[00:01:18] Lena Morales: likely the Private control plane over PrivateLink, because we still want logs shipped to our SIEM but no direct internet from inference nodes.
[00:01:36] Tom Wu: and for throughput, we expect bursts of 200 qps with typical prompt lengths around 120 tokens, sometimes large batches for embeddings.
[00:02:00] Samira Khan: okay that helps. on the runtime side, the big levers for latency/throughput are: model quantization (INT8/FP16), batching windows, and KV cache placement. if you colocate the KV cache with the model workers you get lowest RTTs for cache hits, but it increases replication needs.
[00:02:34] Amira Lopez: quick security note, we need KMS integration for encryption at rest and key access logs.
[00:02:46] Jordan Park: absolutely; Redwood Private supports customer KMS in the control plane and you can point the runtime at customer-managed CMKs, logs published to CloudWatch or your S3 audit bucket via role. we'll share the docs.
[00:03:10] [Speaker 1]: so on PrivateLink, the standard pattern is a cross-account endpoint service in Redwood account, we create an endpoint service for the control plane, you create an interface endpoint in your VPC. this keeps control plane traffic inside AWS and avoids NAT.
[00:03:40] Lena Morales: how do we do model artifact pull? we need the model weights to be pulled from our S3 in the same VPC.
[00:03:52] Samira Khan: we support two patterns: 1) pre-stage artifacts into the runtime-local storage via a sidecar sync that pulls from your S3 over VPC endpoints, or 2) we run a data-plane pull over PrivateLink to a customer-managed artifact endpoint. Option 1 is best for air-gapped or strict egress.
[00:04:18] Raj Patel: sidecar sync sounds promising. any concerns about initial warm-up time?
[00:04:26] Samira Khan: yeah the first load will hit cold-starts, you should plan warmers or pre-warm the model and KV cache. warm-start for KV often reduces p99 by 30-50% depending on hit rate.
[00:04:52] Jordan Park: and to add, for multi-AZ failover, PrivateLink endpoints are AZ-specific ENIs; we recommend provisioning interface endpoints in each AZ where you plan to run inference. that gives failover without Internet egress.
[00:05:20] Lena Morales: okay, what about NAT? our security team typically blocks outbound internet egress and prefers using NAT with egress logging. can we still do auto updates?
[00:05:34] Jordan Park: if you block internet egress, you'll either use controlled egress via NAT plus a limited allowlist for our control plane OR disable direct outbound and use PrivateLink for all control-plane interactions. for updates, with no internet we recommend the sidecar sync approach and manual coordination for runtime updates.
[00:06:02] Tom Wu: ENI limits per subnet worry me. we run many pods per node and don't have a huge quota. what's recommended?
[00:06:12] Samira Khan: recommended is larger /20 or /19 subnets for inference zones; also consider using CNI with trunking or secondary IP ranges for high pod density, that reduces ENI pressure. we can provide a sample sizing calc.
[00:06:40] Raj Patel: does Redwood require route table changes for PrivateLink?
[00:06:45] Jordan Park: interface endpoints don't require route table edits; they create ENIs with private IPs. for Transit Gateway patterns we may need route table entries to steer traffic to the TGW. we'll share a diagram.
[00:07:10] [00:07:10] Samira Khan: switching to runtime perf, for KV cache placement-- colocation gives microsecond-level access to KV; remote cache over PrivateLink adds 1-3ms depending on AZ hops and PrivateLink lat. for chat p99 budgets, that can be material.
[00:07:36] Lena Morales: what's Redwood's KV store technology? is it redis or a custom store?
[00:07:44] Samira Khan: we typically use a tuned redis-compatible in-memory store; in Private we can set up customer-managed Redis inside the VPC or run Redwood's managed cache behind PrivateLink. there are tradeoffs: customer Redis gives you control but you handle HA, shards, and persistence.
[00:08:08] Amira Lopez: we prefer to manage the cache for auditability.
[00:08:12] Jordan Park: that's fine; we'll document recommended configs for replication and instance sizes per model QPS.
[00:08:28] [00:08:28] Raj Patel: on batching, if we batch aggressively, we get better throughput but p99 latency increases, right?
[00:08:36] Samira Khan: correct. Redwood runtime has adaptive batching; you can set a latency SLO and target batch size. for example, set target latency 120ms and we'll flush batches to meet that. for embeddings where latency is less critical you can increase batch windows for throughput.
[00:09:02] Tom Wu: can we pin certain model variants to dedicated nodes? we want predictable p99s for critical routes.
[00:09:10] Samira Khan: yes, you can pin routes to Dedicated pools or node groups. in Private mode we allow node pool labeling and tenant isolation. that gives you predictable tail latencies.
[00:09:28] Lena Morales: walk me through DNS. we have split-horizon DNS internally, will Redwood expect public names?
[00:09:36] Jordan Park: for control plane we use endpoints and hostnames that can be resolved via your VPC Resolver or private hosted zone. we recommend Route53 private hosted zones with records for redwood-control.<your-domain>. the runtime can be configured to use your DNS resolvers so nothing leaks to public.
[00:09:58] Raj Patel: what about certificate management for mTLS?
[00:10:04] Samira Khan: we support mTLS using customer certs; control plane connections are TLS and you can supply certs or integrate with your ACME/KMS. we'll include a cert rotation doc.
[00:10:20] [00:10:20] Amira Lopez: SOC2 scope question: do logs from the runtime flow to Redwood or stay in our account?
[00:10:30] Priya Desai: logs can stay in your account. we can ship a minimal telemetry set to Redwood for health signals if you allow it, but full audit logs and request payloads can be kept on your side.
[00:10:50] Raj Patel: switching back to perf: quantization — how stable are INT8 models for generation quality? we've seen regressions.
[00:11:00] Samira Khan: yes INT8 can introduce small quality regressions; we recommend FP16 for many generative tasks and INT8 for embedding or where throughput matters. Redwood Optimize can run evals on your prompts to measure quality regressions; we'll share a sample eval report.
[00:11:28] Tom Wu: what's the expected p50/p95/p99 improvement if we move from FP16 to INT8?
[00:11:36] Samira Khan: depends on model and hardware; rough numbers: INT8 can give 1.8-2.5x throughput improvement and per-token latency reduced by 20-40% on some kernels, but p99 depends on batching behavior and cache hit rates.
[00:11:58] [00:11:58] Jordan Park: note that certain kernels may require CPU fallback for specific ops and that can increase tail if not profiled. that's why our compile+kernel selection stage matters; we'll share model-specific profiles.
[00:12:20] Raj Patel: can we run A/B rollouts for quantized versus non-quantized variants?
[00:12:26] Samira Khan: yes, rollout policies support canary and A/B testing with automatic fallback to a higher fidelity variant if quality falls below thresholds.
[00:12:40] Lena Morales: network egress again: if we use PrivateLink and block all NAT egress, how do we get OS and security updates for nodes?
[00:12:50] Jordan Park: typical approach is an update window where nodes are allowed egress to specific update endpoints via NAT; alternatively you can manage bastion-backed updates or pre-bake images in your AMI pipeline. we recommend documented maintenance windows and allowlists.
[00:13:12] Tom Wu: any special considerations for GPU instance types and ENI attachment?
[00:13:20] Samira Khan: GPU instances have same ENI semantics; for high density we recommend using Amazon EKS with trunking or Karpenter-style scaling to reduce per-node ENI needs. also watch for instance credits and thermal throttling for sustained load.
[00:13:44] [00:13:44] Raj Patel: do you have suggested Monitoring dashboards? we need token-level cost and tail latency.
[00:13:52] Priya Desai: yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route p50/p95/p99, KV hit rates, and model-level throughput. for Private we can ship the metrics to your CloudWatch or Prometheus endpoint.
[00:14:10] Amira Lopez: if we keep logs in our account, does Redwood still get enough telemetry to support debug?
[00:14:18] Jordan Park: we can collect minimal anonymized traces with your opt-in to help debug while preserving payload privacy. we also support redacted logging for request metadata.
[00:14:36] [00:14:36] Samira Khan: practical recommendation: colocate KV cache in at least one AZ and use cross-AZ replication for failover; set batching latency targets on critical routes to 100ms and non-critical to 250-500ms; pre-warm KV cache during deployments; use FP16 for gen paths initially and run evals for INT8 to judge quality.
[00:15:10] Lena Morales: can you share an exact network diagram?
[00:15:14] Jordan Park: yes we'll share a diagram showing PrivateLink endpoints per AZ, sample route tables, sidecar sync flow and S3 endpoint patterns.
[00:15:28] Raj Patel: on billing: how does Redwood charge for Private—same usage plus infra fee?
[00:15:34] Jordan Park: Private has a platform fee plus usage similar to hosted; for Dedicated/pinned capacity we'll provide a reserved commit quote. we'll send a pricing sheet.
[00:15:50] [00:15:50] Tom Wu: any gotchas with Transit Gateway?
[00:15:56] Samira Khan: TGW works, but route table complexity can add overhead; also check for overlapping CIDRs because TGW doesn't handle NAT for overlapping ranges well.
[00:16:20] Raj Patel: can we do a POC with 2 AZs and a small workload?
[00:16:26] Jordan Park: yes absolutely, typical POC runs 2 AZs, one model, traffic replay for 24-72 hours. we'll scope the SLOs and sample prompts.
[00:16:44] [00:16:44] Amira Lopez: compliance question: do you provide attestations for KMS rotation and key provenance?
[00:16:52] Priya Desai: we provide the controls mapping for SOC2 and can share the security playbook; for Private deployments, key control remains with you.
[00:17:08] Samira Khan: quick note on KV hit rate measurement: instrument your warmers and measure effective token reuse. typical chat workloads get 40-70% KV hit rates with good prefix caching which dramatically helps p99.
[00:17:34] Raj Patel: if we see large p99 spikes, what's the standard remediation?
[00:17:40] Jordan Park: immediate steps are to check KV hit rates, batch sizes, and node pool saturation; we can on-call to run a hotfix or scale node pools.
[00:17:54] [00:17:54] Tom Wu: do you support eBPF-based egress control? our security team likes eBPF airflow filters.
[00:18:02] Samira Khan: we don't manage eBPF agents for you, but Redwood runtime is compatible with host-level eBPF controls; you'll want to test packet capture and performance.
[00:18:18] Lena Morales: can you share the model compile profile for our target model?
[00:18:24] Samira Khan: yes, we'll provide the kernel selection profile and recommended instance types for that model; we might need a sample model or the model name.
[00:18:40] Raj Patel: ok we'll share the model name and sample prompt set.
[00:18:46] Jordan Park: next steps recap: Redwood to share network diagram, PrivateLink config, KV cache sizing guide, benchmarks; Acme to share CIDR and model info and we schedule a POC.
[00:19:10] [00:19:10] Samira Khan: any final clarifying questions on batching or quantization?
[00:19:18] Tom Wu: can you give a rule of thumb for batch size vs latency?
[00:19:24] Samira Khan: rule of thumb: smaller batch sizes (<8) keep latency low for chat; larger batches (32-128) for embeddings give much higher throughput. adaptive batching optimizes dynamically.
[00:19:44] Raj Patel: thanks, we also want a note on how to roll back quantized variants if quality drops mid-run.
[00:19:52] Samira Khan: rollbacks are supported via rollout policies and immediate fallback triggers.
[00:20:04] [00:20:04] Jordan Park: okay let's pause there; we'll follow up with the doc bundle and schedule the POC kickoff. thanks all.
